model.description: Provider model id of the THINKING model; the template carries ctx.model (strict, resolved at instantiation). Convention (K-H2): pass a RESOLVED literal. R-CG-1: the core is allowed to take longer than the channel voice, so the shipped timeouts are the long ones - a channel-voice model here wastes the split.

description.purpose: The agent core's one inference (R-CG-1): reasoning, LLM-backed tool work and everything a channel voice hands over. Its system state - identity, core instructions, tool schemas, the memory bundle of the central hive - accumulates in its own cell.db, one writer per system path.
description.use_when: Inside the cogny composite, behind the collector's seam. Slower and stronger than a talky brain on purpose; the whole point of the advisor split is that nobody waits for this call.
description.not_in_scope: No tool execution, no context assembly, no channel persona. Cogny never speaks to a user directly - it answers the channel voice, which verbalises the result in its own tone. Provider and auth are instance business: the shipped default is the OpenRouter chat lane, a subscription or another provider is override_params.
description.emits_meaning: finish_reason 'stop'/'tool_calls' -> ./split (the dispatcher tells a final answer from a tool bundle); 'length' -> the collector's in_answer lane (a truncated answer is an answer); 'error'/'content_filter' -> the parent's drain, wired from ./brain, because an error echo carries the PROMPT back and must never be filed as the core's own words.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[] the assembled errand of one consultation - the talky IS this brain's user. A body with system but WITHOUT messages is a system update: it upserts the slot and triggers no inference.
examples: a consult errand -> tool_calls -> the core's own tool round -> the same seam again with iter+1 -> stop, and the advice leaves on the answer lane
a consultation the core cannot finish alone -> stop with a question, which travels the SAME return lane and reaches the user through the channel voice
